observation.visible_scene: A clear glass/crystal sphere rests on a band of wet, rounded pebbles at the edge of a calm lake or sea during sunset. The sun sits low on the horizon to the right, throwing a bright vertical glitter path across the water and onto the wet stones in the foreground. The sphere contains an inverted, refracted image of the same horizon and sky, with a bright sun-reflection streak near its left side. The sky is warm orange-pink with thin clouds, and a low dark shoreline is visible across the water.
visible_changes: The crystal sphere stays fixed in position and orientation on the pebbles throughout the excerpt; no translation, rotation, or deformation of the sphere is observed.
Small waves and ripples continuously lap and recede over the foreground pebbles, so the waterline around the stones and the wet sheen on them shift from frame to frame.
The sun's glitter path on the open water and the reflected highlights on the wet stones shimmer and change shape as the surface moves.
The bright refracted sun-streak inside the sphere flickers slightly in intensity as the external water surface moves, but its position within the sphere remains essentially constant.
The sun, horizon line, distant land, and cloud pattern remain essentially stationary across the segment.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the sphere was placed on the shore and whether it remains there after the clip ends.
Whether the overall water level (tide/wave set) is rising or falling beyond this short window.
The exact cause of the small surface ripples (wind vs. wave action), which is not visible.
uncertain_details: Camera motion: the framing of the sphere and horizon appears fixed, so the clip is most consistent with a static shot, but only the limited background evidence is available to confirm this.

The precise direction and pattern of the lapping water are hard to track frame-by-frame; what is clearly supported is only that the near-surface water and its reflections are in gentle, ongoing motion.
